every run is codex:gpt-6.1-terra at its requested level (Extra high as xhigh) on Codex CLI 0.159.0 with the workspace-write sandbox, from bench/2026-10-27-gpt61-terra-frontier-v4 with a clean source block and every task hash equal to the frozen suite lock
every integrity audit: no web, no benchmark data or answer-key paths, not contaminated

each run's token totals equal its Codex receipt, whose stream hash equals the archived stream; every run's API-equivalent cost recomputed at the published list rates and matched to the sweep's run-time stamp
the Codex model-metadata fallback notice appears in exactly three runs (extra-high hedgecore, pacecore and tallycore), each of which passed its tests
the population record's hash and the manifest's hash equal the ones frozen in the protocol, and every run's summary hash equals its manifest entry

rubric, prompts, schemas, seed, repeats, gate allowance, weights, retry rule, control hashes, both judges' settings and the Muse binary equal the published v3.24 record; the settings equal the recovered v3.3 and v3.4 protocols, whose hashes match the published values; the Cursor pin names version 2026.10.01-e373342 and its frozen directory digest, recomputed on this host when present

both judges passed calibration under v3.29 (Muse Spark 1.3 with the one-gate allowance on g11, Grok 4.6 on every gate); no reviewer fallback; every selected Grok call records the accepted display rename
no live operator marker; the one superseded marker is Muse's settlecore probe, published through recover_escaped_excerpts with one excerpt respelled, and its match call made

per-row Code quality, both combined scores and each judge's single-judge score recomputed and matched to the frozen summary, with intent recovery redistributed where no quirk family passed; each level's means and standard errors, per-judge means included, matched to the summary's groups

combined score, its standard error, Code quality, tasks passed, minutes and cost per level matched to the harness card table; the card is byte-identical to the harness copy and its record names this summary and the comparator tables
no dashes, NUL characters or host paths in exported text
limits: Muse Spark 1.3's intent probe of max settlecore is published through the owner-approved recover_escaped_excerpts rule (owner decision 2026-10-29): both attempts had decoded the escapes in one quoted byte-string line into control characters, and the rule wrote them back as the source spells them. The rule first spelled NUL only as backslash-zero, so the probe was marked invalid and the first summary published 114 of 115; the rule now also tries backslash-x-00, and the summary was rebuilt.
Muse Spark 1.3 passed calibration with the one-gate allowance: repeatability (g11) fell 0.26 short, within the half-point the protocol allows for one gate.
Three extra-high runs printed Codex's notice that it had no model metadata for gpt-6.1-terra and used fallback metadata; all three passed every hidden test, and they stay in the population.
Model identity is requested-only: Codex does not report the serving model.
The sweep ran on release day plus one, through Codex CLI 0.159.0 pinned by version; it cannot pin what OpenAI serves under the model id.
Frontier Code quality is the reviewed layer plus intent recovery and is never compared with Routine v1 Code quality.
One attempt per task and level, on the owner's Mac, local sandbox, flat 3-hour task bound, one task at a time.
publication_scope: Per-run scores, per-panel sub-scores, aggregates, judge protocol text, calibration verdicts and control means, integrity-audit verdicts, raw tokens and API-equivalent cost estimates.
withheld: quirk answer keys (they describe hidden-test behaviour)
reviewer session identifiers and usage receipts
solver event streams (a structure-only redacted trace of every run is public in the vulcanbench-gpt61-terra-traces repository)
integrity_limit: Hash checks bind the export to frozen files; they do not prove that judges were unbiased or that no training overlap exists.
